security_spec.violation_condition: Linux kernel trap handler or KVM reads aceerror CSR bits in non-prioritized order (e.g., checking lower-priority exc.code bits before higher-priority ones) when reporting ACE instruction faults to userspace or virtualizing the CSR for a guest, potentially masking a higher-severity error behind a lower-severity one.
security_spec.summary: aceerror now has a normative error priority table; kernel trap handlers and KVM virtualization must inspect exc.code bits in decreasing priority order (6→5→3(top)→3→2/1→1→3(bottom)→4→0) or risk reporting a masked low-priority error to userspace while a higher-priority error (e.g., Unconfigured CR) remains undiagnosed.

findings.finding: No aceerror or ACEERROR CSR is defined in the kernel. The full set of CSR definitions (lines 251-609) contains no ACE-related error CSR. Without such a CSR, no code can read it in non-prioritized order.
findings.snippet:
#define CSR_CYCLE      0xc00
#define CSR_TIME       0xc01
...
#define CSR_VSTART     0x8
#define CSR_VCSR       0xf
#define CSR_VL          0xc20
#define CSR_VTYPE       0xc21
#define CSR_VLENB       0xc22

findings.finding: Store/AMO access faults are handled via standard scause exception codes (EXC_STORE_ACCESS=7), not via any ACE-specific error CSR. No aceerror read or priority decoding occurs anywhere in the trap path.
findings.snippet:
DO_ERROR_INFO(do_trap_store_fault,
    SIGSEGV, SEGV_ACCERR, "store (or AMO) access fault");

findings.finding: Store/AMO misaligned faults are handled via scause (EXC_STORE_MISALIGNED=6) dispatch, not via any ACE-specific CSR. The misaligned handler uses a simple type enum (MISALIGNED_STORE/LOAD) with no error register decoding needed.
The generic trap error path stores only regs->cause (scause value) into thread.bad_cause and dispatches purely on user/kernel mode. No aceerror CSR is read or prioritized.
KVM's CSR emulation in vcpu_insn.c dispatches CSR reads/writes via generic handlers. No aceerror CSR virtualization or priority-ordered bit checking exists because the CSR itself is not defined.
